title: FRAs, Duration, Convexity & Term Structure Theories

scenes.title: The Over-the-Counter Rate Lock: Introducing FRAs
scenes.purpose: Introduce FRAs as bespoke OTC instruments to lock future borrowing costs
takeaways: FRAs are bespoke OTC contracts designed to lock in an interest rate over a future window
Market convention quotes FRAs as X by Y (e.g., 3x9 denotes 6-month borrowing starting in 3 months)
At inception, agreed rate R_K equals market forward rate R_F, making contract value zero

messages.speaker: novice
messages.text: How can a corporation lock in borrowing rates for a future 6-month loan starting in 3 months?

messages.speaker: mentor
messages.text: They enter a Forward Rate Agreement (FRA), an OTC contract that guarantees a fixed borrowing rate between two future dates.

messages.speaker: mentor
messages.text: In market terminology, this is a 3 by 9 FRA: borrowing starts at month 3 and matures at month 9, locking the 6-month rate.

messages.speaker: mentor
messages.text: In Part 2, we master FRA pricing, cash settlement discounting, duration immunization, convexity, and term structure theories.

beats.speaker: novice

en.display: How can a corporation lock in borrowing rates for a future 6-month loan starting in 3 months?

hi.display: अगर किसी कंपनी को 3 महीने बाद 6 महीने के लिए लोन लेना हो, तो वो आज ही इंटरेस्ट रेट कैसे लॉक कर सकती है?

beats.onScreenIntent: Opening dilemma question on forward rate hedging

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In Part One, we mastered how zero curves and forward rates are constructed. But how does an institution lock in borrowing or lending rates today for a future period? The standard over-the-counter solution is the Forward Rate Agreement, or FRA.

hi.display: Part One mein humne dekha ki zero curve aur forward rates kaise calculate hote hain. Lekin agar kisi company ko future mein cash borrow ya invest karna ho, toh wo aaj interest rate ko kaise lock karegi? Is problem ka standard over-the-counter solution hai: Forward Rate Agreement, yaani FRA.

beats.onScreenIntent: The mentor connects zero curves to forward contract rate locks

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: An FRA is a bespoke over-the-counter contract between two financial institutions that fixes the interest rate applied to a specified future borrowing or lending horizon.

hi.display: FRA do financial institutions ke beech ek OTC contract hota hai, jisme ek agreed fixed interest rate par specified future time period ke liye borrowing ya lending rate lock kiya jata hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: The mentor defines FRA bilateral mechanics and principal

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In market convention, an FRA is quoted as X by Y. For example, a three-by-nine FRA begins three months from today and ends nine months from today, locking the borrowing cost over a six-month interest period.

hi.display: Market convention mein ise aksar X cross Y FRA kaha jata hai. Jaise Three cross Nine FRA ka matlab hai ki contract aaj se teen mahine baad shuru hoga aur nau mahine par khatam hoga, yaani borrowing period total chhe mahine ka hoga.

beats.onScreenIntent: The mentor explains market quotation convention X by Y

scenes.title: FRA Mechanics: Payer vs. Receiver Profiles
scenes.purpose: Contrast Fixed Rate Payer (borrower hedge) and Fixed Rate Receiver (lender hedge)
takeaways: Fixed Rate Payer pays R_K and receives floating R_M (hedges against rising interest rates)
Fixed Rate Receiver pays floating R_M and receives fixed R_K (hedges against falling interest rates)
Payoffs are zero-sum between counterparties, with cash settlement settling the net difference

left.heading: Fixed Rate Payer (Borrower)
points: Agrees to pay fixed contract rate R_K and receive floating benchmark R_M
Protects against rising borrowing costs on future debt issuance
Profits when market rate R_M exceeds agreed fixed rate R_K at expiration

right.heading: Fixed Rate Receiver (Lender)
points: Agrees to pay floating benchmark R_M and receive fixed contract rate R_K
Protects cash investors and lenders against falling interest yields
Profits when market rate R_M drops below agreed fixed rate R_K at expiration

verdict.text: Fixed payer locks maximum borrowing cost; fixed receiver guarantees minimum investment yield.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: An FRA transaction involves two counterparties: the Fixed Rate Payer and the Fixed Rate Receiver.

hi.display: FRA mein do parties hoti hain: Fixed Rate Payer aur Fixed Rate Receiver.

beats.onScreenIntent: Introduce the two counterparties in an FRA transaction

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The fixed payer pays the agreed fixed rate R_K and receives the floating market benchmark. Corporate borrowers enter this position to hedge against the risk of rising future interest rates.

hi.display: Payer party agreed fixed rate R K pay karti hai aur floating market rate receive karti hai. Ye position wo corporate borrower leta hai jo future mein interest rates badhne ke darr se apna borrowing cost lock karna chahta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Examine Fixed Rate Payer payoff profile and protection

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Conversely, the fixed receiver pays the floating market rate and receives the agreed fixed rate R_K. Asset managers and institutional lenders enter this position to lock in yields and guard against falling interest rates.

hi.display: Doosri taraf, Fixed Rate Receiver floating rate pay karke fixed rate receive karta hai. Ye position asset managers aur lenders lete hain jo future mein interest rates girne ke risk se apne returns ko protect karna chahte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Examine Fixed Rate Receiver payoff profile and cash settlement

scenes.title: The FRA Cash Settlement Formula & In-Advance Discounting
scenes.purpose: Derive in-advance FRA cash settlement discounting formula
takeaways: FRA payoffs normally earned at T2 are settled at T1 when borrowing begins
Cash settlement requires discounting by [1 + R_M * (T2 - T1)] back to T1
Payoff = L * (R_M - R_K) * (T2 - T1) / [1 + R_M * (T2 - T1)]

data.title: FRA In-Advance Cash Settlement Payoff Formula

variables.meaning: Actual Realized Market Rate at T1

parts.meaning: In-advance discount divisor to date T1

data.note: Settlement occurs at date T1 rather than T2, requiring division by the spot money market factor.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Crucially, cash settlement for an FRA occurs at expiration time T-one—the exact start of the borrowing period—rather than at maturity T-two when the loan concludes.

hi.display: FRA ka cash settlement expiration date T-one par hota hai, yaani borrowing period shuru hone par, na ki period ke end T-two par.

beats.onScreenIntent: Explain why cash settlement occurs at inception date T1

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: If the market floating rate fixes at R_M and the agreed fixed rate is R_K, the cash flow paid to the fixed payer equals principal L, multiplied by R_M minus R_K times the time interval, divided by one plus R_M times the time interval.

hi.display: Agar market floating rate R M ho aur agreed rate R K ho, toh payer ko milne wala cash flow hai: principal L guna R M minus R K guna time interval, divided by one plus R M guna time interval.

beats.onScreenIntent: Formulate the exact FRA payoff formula with discount divisor

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The presence of one plus R_M times the time interval in the denominator is essential: because loan interest is normally paid in arrears at time T-two, settling the cash compensation in advance at time T-one requires discounting by the prevailing market interest rate.

hi.display: Denominator mein one plus R M guna time interval isliye aata hai kyunki interest ka actual payment T-two par hona tha, lekin cash compensation T-one par advance mein de diya jata hai. Isliye is payoff ko discount karna mandatory hota hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Walk through economic intuition of in-advance cash discounting

scenes.title: Valuing an Existing FRA Prior to Maturity
scenes.purpose: Calculate mark-to-market value of an existing FRA using current forward rates
takeaways: Prior to expiration, FRA value is determined by comparing R_K with forward rate R_F
Future cash flow difference is discounted back using continuous zero discount factor e^(-R_2*T_2)

data.title: Mark-to-Market Valuation of an Existing FRA
data.conclusion: The fixed rate payer has an unrealized mark-to-market gain of $477,999 because market borrowing rates rose above the locked rate.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: After inception, as the market zero curve shifts, how do we calculate the mark-to-market fair value of an existing FRA?

hi.display: Contract enter karne ke baad, market zero curve change hone par FRA ki fair market value kaise calculate hoti hai?

beats.onScreenIntent: Formulate mark to market valuation equation for existing FRAs

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Under John Hull's formulation, we determine the current forward rate R_F, compute the interest differential relative to R_K, and discount the payoff from maturity T-two back to today using the zero rate R-two: value V equals L times R_F minus R_K times T-two minus T-one, multiplied by e raised to minus R-two times T-two.

hi.display: Hull ke mutabik, current forward rate R F aur agreed rate R K ke difference ko calculate karke use maturity T-two ke zero rate se present value par discount kiya jata hai: V barabar L guna R F minus R K guna T-two minus T-one guna e to the power minus R-two T-two.

beats.onScreenIntent: Walk through numerical parameters for $100M FRA valuation

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: At contract inception, the agreed fixed rate R_K is set precisely equal to the current market forward rate R_F, ensuring the initial theoretical value of the FRA is exactly zero.

hi.display: Jab contract freshly enter hota hai, toh R K ko exact forward rate R F ke barabar set kiya jata hai, jisse FRA ki initial value exactly zero hoti hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Calculate continuous present value and conclude with gain

scenes.title: Macaulay Duration: The Weighted Average Horizon
scenes.purpose: Define Macaulay duration as cash flow weighted maturity
takeaways: Macaulay duration measures the effective time needed to recover bond cash flows
Zero-coupon bonds have Macaulay duration exactly equal to maturity T
Coupon payments pull cash flow weights earlier, reducing duration below maturity

cards.title: Cash Flow Weighted Maturity
cards.body: Macaulay duration weights each cash flow date t_i by the present value proportion of that cash flow relative to total bond price B.

cards.title: Zero-Coupon Benchmark
cards.body: For a zero-coupon bond paying full principal at maturity T, Macaulay duration equals maturity T exactly (D = T).

cards.title: Coupon Pull Effect
cards.body: Because coupon bonds distribute cash flows prior to maturity, their Macaulay duration is strictly less than their maturity horizon.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Now we examine the core quantitative metric of fixed income risk management: Duration, formulated by Frederick Macaulay in nineteen thirty-eight.

hi.display: Ab aate hain fixed income risk management ke core concept par: Duration. Frederick Macaulay ne nineteen thirty-eight mein introduce kiya tha ki bond ki maturity sirf uski final date nahi hoti.

beats.onScreenIntent: Define Macaulay duration and weighted cash flow concept

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Macaulay Duration measures the weighted average time until all bond cash flows are received, where each future payment date is weighted by its relative present discounted value.

hi.display: Macaulay Duration batata hai ki bond ke cash flows ko receive karne mein average kitna time lagta hai, jahan har cash flow ke time ko uski present value se weight kiya jata hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Contrast zero coupon duration against coupon bond duration

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: For a zero-coupon bond, duration equals its stated maturity exactly. But for a coupon-bearing bond, duration is always strictly less than final maturity, because intermediate coupon payments return capital earlier.

hi.display: Zero-coupon bond ki duration exactly uski maturity ke barabar hoti hai. Lekin coupon bond ki duration hamesha uski maturity se kam hoti hai kyunki intermediate coupons jaldi receive ho jate hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Summarize how coupon size and yield affect effective maturity

scenes.title: Modified Duration & Price Sensitivity
scenes.purpose: Formulate Modified duration as first-order percentage price sensitivity
takeaways: Modified duration D* = D / (1 + y/m) measures price sensitivity directly
First-order price response: Delta B / B ≈ -D* * Delta y
Higher duration implies greater capital vulnerability to interest rate increases

data.title: Modified Duration Price Sensitivity Equation

variables.meaning: Parallel Shift in Yield to Maturity

parts.meaning: Modified duration adjusted for discrete compounding
Inverse price-yield direction (yield up -> price down)
Percentage capital change in portfolio value

data.note: Modified duration provides a linear first-order approximation accurate for small yield shocks.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Duration is far more than an effective maturity measure; it is the primary linear metric of interest rate price sensitivity: the percentage change in bond price equals minus Modified Duration D-star, multiplied by the yield change delta y.

hi.display: Duration sirf time measure nahi hai; ye interest rate sensitivity ka primary formula hai. Percentage price change barabar minus D star guna delta y.

beats.onScreenIntent: Introduce Modified duration and differentiate from Macaulay form

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Under continuous compounding, Modified Duration D-star is mathematically identical to Macaulay Duration D. This indicates that a one percent increase in market yields causes an immediate D percent decline in bond price.

hi.display: Continuous compounding mein Modified Duration D star exactly Macaulay Duration D ke barabar hota hai. Formula batata hai ki agar yield one percent badhti hai, toh bond ka price approximately D percent se drop ho jayega.

beats.onScreenIntent: Formulate percentage price move equation Delta B / B ≈ -D* Delta y

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Portfolio managers utilize this principle to immunize balance sheets against parallel yield curve shifts, aligning asset duration with liability duration to neutralize net equity exposure.

hi.display: Portfolio manager apne total asset duration aur liability duration ko match karke balance sheet ko parallel interest rate shifts se immunize kar sakta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Explain portfolio immunization: matching asset and liability duration

scenes.title: Convexity: Correcting the Linear Approximation
scenes.purpose: Illustrate second-order curvature correction via Convexity
takeaways: Duration is a linear tangent approximation that underestimates price gains and overestimates drops
Convexity C = (1/B)*(d^2 B/dy^2) measures curvature of the price-yield relationship
Full Taylor expansion: Delta B / B ≈ -D* * Delta y + 0.5 * C * (Delta y)^2

cells: Linear tangent; accurate only for infinitesimal yield moves (e.g., < 10 bps)
Delta B / B ≈ -D* * Delta y + 0.5 * C * (Delta y)^2
Captures curvature; highly accurate for large market rate shocks (e.g., > 100 bps)
Bonds gain more when yields fall than they lose when yields rise by same amount

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: However, duration is only a first-order linear approximation. In reality, the fundamental relationship between bond price and yield is a curved, convex trajectory.

hi.display: Lekin duration ek linear approximation hai. Real world mein bond price aur yield ka graph straight line nahi, balki convex curve hota hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Explain the limitation of linear duration for large rate shocks

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: When interest rates experience substantial shocks, linear duration overestimates price declines and underestimates price gains. This curvature error is corrected by Convexity C, the second derivative of price with respect to yield.

hi.display: Jab yield mein bada change aata hai, toh duration price change ko underestimate karta hai. Is error ko correct karta hai Convexity C, jo price-yield curve ka second derivative hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Present the second order Taylor series expansion including convexity

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The full Taylor series expansion states that percentage price change approximately equals minus D times delta y, plus one-half C times delta y squared. Because convexity is strictly positive for standard bonds, it cushions losses when yields rise and magnifies gains when yields fall.

hi.display: Taylor series approximation dekhiye: delta B divided by B barabar minus D guna delta y plus half C guna delta y ka square. Convexity hamesha positive hoti hai, isliye yield badhne par price kam girta hai aur yield girne par price zyada badhta hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Explain why positive convexity is inherently desirable for investors

scenes.title: Theories of the Term Structure: Expectations vs. Segmentation
scenes.purpose: Contrast Expectations Theory and Market Segmentation Theory
takeaways: Expectations Theory states forward rates equal expected future spot zero rates
Market Segmentation Theory asserts supply and demand within maturity buckets dictate rates
Neither theory alone explains why yield curves are predominantly upward-sloping

cards.title: Expectations Theory
cards.body: Hypothesizes that long-term interest rates reflect market consensus forecasts of future short-term rates. Assumes investors are risk-neutral across maturities.

cards.title: Market Segmentation Theory
cards.body: Argues institutional investors (like pension funds vs commercial banks) have rigid maturity preferences, creating independent supply-demand equilibria in each bucket.

cards.title: The Empirical Gap
cards.body: Expectations theory implies curves should slope downward as often as upward; empirical reality shows upward slopes occur > 85% of the time.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Yield curves exhibit varying shapes across market cycles: upward sloping, flat, or inverted. Three classical economic theories explain the morphology of the term structure.

hi.display: Yield curve ka shape kabhi upward hota hai, kabhi flat aur kabhi inverted. Is term structure ko explain karne ke liye teen classical economic theories hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Introduce theories explaining the shape of the yield curve

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The Expectations Theory asserts that long-term interest rates equal the pure mathematical average of expected future short-term rates. Under this hypothesis, an upward-sloping yield curve implies the market expects short rates to rise.

hi.display: Pehli theory hai Expectations Theory: Ye manti hai ki long-term rate market ke expected future short-term rates ka pure average hota hai. Is theory ke mutabik, upward curve ka matlab hai ki market short rates badhne ki expectation kar raha hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Explain Expectations Theory assumptions and implications

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: In contrast, Market Segmentation Theory contends that institutional investors operate in rigid maturity silos. Pension funds buy thirty-year paper while corporate treasurers buy short-term bills, with zero cross-maturity substitution.

hi.display: Doosri theory hai Market Segmentation Theory: Ye assume karti hai ki alag-alag maturity markets completely independent hote hain. Pension funds long-term bonds khareedte hain aur banks short-term paper, aur inke beech koi switching nahi hoti.

beats.onScreenIntent: Introduce Market Segmentation Theory and maturity clienteles

scenes.title: Liquidity Preference Theory: Why Curves Slope Upward
scenes.purpose: Explain Liquidity Preference Theory and liquidity premium mechanics
takeaways: Borrowers prefer locking long-term debt while investors prefer liquid short-term assets
Borrowers must pay a liquidity premium to induce investors to hold long-term debt
Forward rates exceed expected future spot rates: R_F = E(spot) + Liquidity Premium

links.text: Lenders seek short-term liquidity while corporate borrowers demand long-term funding
Long-term borrowers must offer higher yields to incentivize investors to surrender liquidity
A positive liquidity risk premium is embedded across ascending maturity horizons
Forward rates systematically exceed market expectations of future spot zero rates
Produces the persistently upward-sloping yield curve observed in global bond markets

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: John C. Hull identifies Liquidity Preference Theory as the most realistic and robust explanation of empirical yield curve behavior.

hi.display: John C. Hull Liquidity Preference Theory ko real-world markets ka sabse accurate model mante hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Introduce Liquidity Preference Theory to resolve empirical gaps

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Investors naturally value liquidity and demand a positive term premium to lock up capital over long horizons. Conversely, corporate borrowers prefer long-term fixed borrowing to eliminate rollover refinancing risk.

hi.display: Investors natural liquidity prefer karte hain aur long-term capital lock karne ke liye ek positive Liquidity Premium demand karte hain. Doosri taraf, borrowers refinancing risk se bachne ke liye long-term fixed borrowing chahte hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Explain maturity mismatch between borrowers and lenders

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Because of this structural imbalance, forward rates equal expected future spot rates plus a positive liquidity premium. This term premium explains why normal sovereign yield curves slope naturally upward.

hi.display: Is asymmetric preference ki wajah se Forward Rate hamesha Expected Future Spot Rate plus Liquidity Premium ke barabar hota hai. Yahi reason hai ki normal conditions mein yield curve naturally upward sloping hoti hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Prove why forward rates exceed expected future spot rates

scenes.title: Active Recall Scenario: Calculating Bond Price Move via Duration
scenes.purpose: Test understanding of Modified duration percentage price move calculation
takeaways: Percentage price move: Delta B / B = -D* * Delta y
A 5-year duration bond drops by 2.5% when yields rise by 50 basis points
Sign check: yield increase always produces negative capital return

data.question: A bond portfolio has a modified duration of 5.0 years. If interest rate yields rise by 50 basis points (+0.50%), what is the approximate percentage price change?
data.explanation: Delta B / B ≈ -D* * Delta y = -5.0 * (+0.0050) = -0.0250 (-2.50%). Option C is correct.

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Let us test your fixed income risk calculation skills. Suppose a bond portfolio has a Modified Duration of six point zero years and a market value of one hundred million dollars. If interest rates rise by fifty basis points, or point five zero percent, what is the estimated dollar price change?

hi.display: Chaliye ek practical risk calculation test karte hain. Ek bond portfolio ki Modified Duration six point zero years hai aur portfolio value one hundred million dollars hai. Agar interest rates fifty basis points badh jate hain, toh portfolio price change kitna hoga?

beats.onScreenIntent: Present the student with active recall duration question

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: Apply the duration sensitivity formula: percentage price change equals minus D-star multiplied by delta y. Pause and consider the options.

hi.display: Formula apply kijiye: percentage change barabar minus D star guna delta y. Pause and consider.

beats.onScreenIntent: Work through algebraic calculation: -5.0 * 0.0050 = -2.50%

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The correct answer is Option B: minus three point zero percent, representing a loss of three million dollars. Calculating directly: minus six point zero times positive point zero zero five zero equals minus point zero three zero, or negative three percent. On a one hundred million dollar portfolio, this produces an exact three million dollar loss.

hi.display: Correct answer hai Option B: Minus three point zero percent loss, yaani minus three million dollars. Calculation: minus six point zero guna positive zero point zero zero five zero barabar minus zero point zero three zero. Hundred million par three percent loss exact three million dollars hota hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Reinforce intuition: inverse price-yield relationship

scenes.title: Case Study: The $1.6B Orange County Bankruptcy
scenes.purpose: Analyze 1994 Orange County collapse due to extreme duration and leverage
takeaways: Orange County geared a $7.5B equity base into a $20B portfolio using reverse repos
Portfolio duration reached ~7.4 years, leaving it defenseless against rate hikes
When the Fed raised rates by 300 bps, collateral calls triggered $1.6B insolvency

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: The ultimate historical catastrophe illustrating the lethal risk of unhedged duration and leverage is the nineteen ninety-four Orange County bankruptcy.

hi.display: Interest rate risk ko underestimate karne par kya anjaam hota hai, iska global history mein sabse bada example hai nineteen ninety-four ka Orange County Bankruptcy.

beats.onScreenIntent: Introduce the 1994 Orange County bankruptcy case study

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: County treasurer Robert Citron leveraged seven point five billion dollars of public funds into a twenty billion dollar portfolio using short-term reverse repurchase agreements, heavily concentrating capital in inverse floating-rate notes.

hi.display: Orange County treasurer Robert Citron ne seven point five billion dollar ke public funds ko reverse repo borrowings ke zariye twenty billion dollars tak heavily leverage kiya, aur sara paisa Inverse Floating-Rate Notes mein invest kar diya.

beats.onScreenIntent: Examine reverse repo leverage structure and duration mismatch

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: When the Federal Reserve raised interest rates aggressively by three hundred basis points throughout nineteen ninety-four, repo borrowing costs skyrocketed while yields on inverse floaters collapsed.

hi.display: Jab nineteen ninety-four mein US Federal Reserve ne rates ko rapidly three hundred basis points badhaya, toh repo borrowing costs shoot up ho gayi aur inverse floaters ke yields collapse ho gaye.

beats.onScreenIntent: Explain Fed 300 bps rate hikes and margin call spiral

beats.speaker: mentor

en.display: This massive duration mismatch triggered massive margin calls, forcing Orange County to realize one point six billion dollars in losses and file the largest municipal bankruptcy in United States history at that time.

hi.display: Is deadly leverage mismatch ne Orange County ko one point six billion dollars ka loss karwaya aur America ki us waqt ki sabse badi municipal bankruptcy file karni padi. Extreme duration aur repo leverage ek deadly combination hote hain.

beats.onScreenIntent: Summarize risk management lessons on leverage and duration limits

scenes.title: Summary Thread: Four Pillars of Fixed Income Risk Management
scenes.purpose: Synthesize the core risk management principles of Chapter 4 Part 2
takeaways: FRAs lock forward borrowing costs with in-advance cash settlement discounting
Modified duration predicts linear price moves and immunizes asset-liability portfolios
Convexity captures second-order curvature essential during large market rate shocks

rules.title: FRA forward locks
rules.text: FRAs are bespoke OTC contracts allowing counterparties to lock borrowing rates over future windows.

rules.title: In-advance cash settlement
rules.text: FRA settlement occurs at date T1, requiring discounting by [1 + R_M * (T2 - T1)] back to inception.

rules.title: Mark-to-market valuation
rules.text: Prior to expiry, FRA value is determined by comparing R_K with forward rate R_F discounted by e^(-R_2*T_2).

rules.title: Macaulay duration horizon
rules.text: Macaulay duration measures the weighted average maturity of all present-value discounted cash flows.

rules.title: Modified duration sensitivity
rules.text: Modified duration D* = D / (1 + y/m) quantifies percentage price move via Delta B / B ≈ -D* * Delta y.

rules.title: Portfolio immunization
rules.text: Matching asset and liability duration immunizes equity against parallel yield curve shifts.

rules.title: Convexity curvature correction
rules.text: Convexity restores precision for large shocks via Delta B / B ≈ -D* * Delta y + 0.5 * C * (Delta y)^2.

rules.title: Liquidity preference premium
rules.text: Borrower demand for long-term debt creates positive liquidity premiums, producing upward-sloping yield curves.

beats.speaker: mentor

hi.display: Aaiye Chapter Four ke final chaar fixed income pillars ko summarize karte hain.

hi.display: Pehla pillar: Forward Rate Agreements. OTC contracts jo future borrowing aur lending rates lock karte hain, jinki settlement T-one par in-advance discount hoti hai.

beats.onScreenIntent: Recap Pillar 2: Macaulay and Modified Duration

hi.display: Dusra pillar: Duration & Immunization. Macaulay duration weighted average maturity hai, aur Modified duration delta B divided by B barabar minus D star delta y se first-order price risk measure karti hai.

hi.display: Teesra pillar: Convexity. Price-yield curve ka curvature jo large rate moves mein duration error ko positive half C delta y square se correct karta hai.
